result.rationale: In the new file, minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Zod object schemas don't support catch-all computed keys this way; both expressions evaluate to the same string (ZodString objects stringify identically), so the second key collides with/overwrites the first and the schema degenerates to just checking `access_token` plus a literal garbage key. The intended permissive validation for credential-sharing mode (accepting arbitrary expiry/extra fields) is broken — a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. These computed keys evaluate to strings (e.g., the `toString()` of Zod types) and are not Zod "catch-all" behavior. Both computed expressions stringify to essentially the same key, so one overwrites the other at object-literal construction time, making the intended “any numeric expiry field + allow other fields” schema ineffective/incorrect. Proper Zod behavior would require `.catchall(...)` / `.passthrough()` / explicit known fields instead of computed keys.
